title: Graph Neural Networks for torch
text: Train GCN PubMed Diabetes citation network document classification. example creates GCN model
code: library(torch) library(torchgnn) library(nanoparquet) library(dplyr)  # read to tempfiles # data from https://linqs.org/datasets/#pubmed-diabetes nodes_tmp <- tempfile("nodes", fileext = ".parquet") edges_tmp <- tempfile("edges", fileext = ".parquet")  download.file(   "https://github.com/JosiahParry/torchgnn/raw/refs/heads/main/examples/data/pubmed-diabetes/edges.parquet",   edges_tmp, quiet = TRUE ) download.file(   "https://github.com/JosiahParry/torchgnn/raw/refs/heads/main/examples/data/pubmed-diabetes/nodes.parquet",   nodes_tmp, quiet = TRUE )  # read in the nodes and edges nodes <- read_parquet(nodes_tmp) edges <- read_parquet(edges_tmp)  # create our adjacency matrix from IDs adj <- adj_from_edgelist(edges$from, edges$to)  # create our training data tensor X <- nodes_to_tensor(   select(nodes, -label),   adj,   node_id = "paper_id" )  # create our target class tensor Y <- nodes_to_tensor(select(nodes, 1:2), adj, "paper_id")$to(   dtype = torch_long() )$squeeze()  # perform a train, test, validation split split <- graph_split(X, seed = 42) # define a 2 layer GCN model model <- model_gcn(   # number of variables   in_features = 500,   # define our hidden layers   hidden_dims = 16,   # predicting 3 labels   out_features = 3,   dropout = 0.5 ) model An `nn_module` containing 8,067 parameters.  ── Modules ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── • layers: <nn_module_list> #8,067 parameters # use ADAM optimizer optimizer <- optim_adam(model$parameters, lr = 0.01)  # set our number of epochs n_epochs <- 100  # create our training loop for (epoch in 1:n_epochs) {   model$train()   optimizer$zero_grad()    out <- model(X, adj)   loss <- nnf_cross_entropy(out[split$train_id, ], Y[split$train_id])    loss$backward()   optimizer$step()    model$eval()   with_no_grad({     val_out <- model(X, adj)     val_pred <- val_out[split$val_id, ]$argmax(dim = 2)     val_acc <- (val_pred == Y[split$val_id])$to(       dtype = torch_float()     )$mean()$item()   })    # print info every 20 epochs   if (epoch %% 20 == 0) {     cat(sprintf(       "Epoch %d | Loss: %.4f | Val Acc: %.4f\n",       epoch,       loss$item(),       val_acc     ))   } } Epoch 20 | Loss: 0.7697 | Val Acc: 0.8085 Epoch 40 | Loss: 0.5386 | Val Acc: 0.8384 Epoch 60 | Loss: 0.4502 | Val Acc: 0.8529 Epoch 80 | Loss: 0.4146 | Val Acc: 0.8623 Epoch 100 | Loss: 0.3883 | Val Acc: 0.8681 model$eval() with_no_grad({   test_out <- model(X, adj)   test_pred <- test_out[split$test_id, ]$argmax(dim = 2)   test_acc <- (test_pred == Y[split$test_id])$to(     dtype = torch_float()   )$mean()$item() })  cat(sprintf("Test Accuracy: %.4f\n", test_acc)) Test Accuracy: 0.8593

title: Normalize an Adjacency Matrix — gcn_normalize
text: Prepare sparse adjacency matrix message passing. gcn_normalize() applies symmetric normalization \(D^{-1/2} D^{-1/2}\) Kipf Welling (2017). adj_row_normalize() applies row normalization \(D^{-1} \), weights node's neighbors sum one. add_graph_self_loops() replaces existing diagonal entries unit self-loops, giving \(+ \). Isolated nodes degree zero. normalization factor set zero rather allowed diverge, contribute nothing aggregation.

what: Graph Attention Network Layer (Veličković et al. 2018) — layer_gat
title: Graph Attention Network Layer (Veličković et al. 2018) — layer_gat
text: Implements Graph Attention Network (GAT) layer: $$\mathbf{h}_i^{(l+1)} = \sigma\left(\sum_{j \\mathcal{N}()} \alpha_{ij} \mathbf{W}^{(l)} \mathbf{h}_j^{(l)}\right)$$ attention coefficients \(\alpha_{ij}\) computed : $$\alpha_{ij} = \frac{\exp(\text{LeakyReLU}(\mathbf{}^T [\mathbf{W}\mathbf{h}_i || \mathbf{W}\mathbf{h}_j]))}{\sum_{k \\mathcal{N}()} \exp(\text{LeakyReLU}(\mathbf{}^T [\mathbf{W}\mathbf{h}_i || \mathbf{W}\mathbf{h}_k]))}$$ layer: Applies linear transformation node features Computes attention coefficients edge Normalizes attention weights via softmax neighbors Aggregates neighbor features weighted attention Parameters: \(W\): in_features x out_features learnable weight matrix \(\): 2 * out_features learnable attention vector

title: Graph Attention Network Layer (Veličković et al. 2018) — layer_gat
code: layer_gat(   in_features,   out_features,   heads = 1,   concat = TRUE,   dropout = 0,   negative_slope = 0.2,   bias = TRUE )

title: Graph Attention Network Layer (Veličković et al. 2018) — layer_gat
text: in_features Integer. Number input features per node out_features Integer. Number output features per node (per head) heads Integer. Number attention heads. Default: 1 concat Logical. TRUE, concatenate multi-head outputs. FALSE, average . Default: TRUE dropout Numeric. Dropout rate (0-1) applied attention coefficients. Default: 0 negative_slope Numeric. Negative slope LeakyReLU. Default: 0.2 bias Logical. Add learnable bias. Default: TRUE

title: Graph Attention Network Layer (Veličković et al. 2018) — layer_gat
text: Tensor n_nodes x (out_features * heads) concat=TRUE, else n_nodes x out_features

title: Graph Attention Network Layer (Veličković et al. 2018) — layer_gat
text: Multi-head attention supported via heads parameter. heads > 1: concat = TRUE: outputs concatenated (output size = out_features * heads) concat = FALSE: outputs averaged (output size = out_features)

title: Graph Attention Network Layer (Veličković et al. 2018) — layer_gat

title: Graph Attention Network Layer (Veličković et al. 2018) — layer_gat
text: Veličković, P., Cucurull, G., Casanova, ., Romero, ., Liò, P., & Bengio, Y. (2018). Graph Attention Networks. International Conference Learning Representations. doi:10.48550/arXiv.1710.10903

title: GCN Convolutional Layer (Kipf & Welling 2016) — layer_gcn
text: \(\tilde{} = \tilde{D}^{-1/2}(+ )\tilde{D}^{-1/2}\) symmetrically normalized adjacency matrix self-loops, \(\tilde{D}\) degree matrix \(+ \). standard GCN layer uses: Single weight matrix \(W\) Symmetric normalization self-loops Optional --fly normalization normalize = TRUE (default), layer computes \(\tilde{}\) --fly input adjacency matrix adding self-loops applying symmetric normalization. normalize = FALSE, must pass pre-normalized adjacency matrix. Parameters: \(W\): in_features x out_features learnable weight matrix \(b\): out_features learnable bias term (optional)

title: GCN Convolutional Layer (Kipf & Welling 2016) — layer_gcn
code: if (FALSE) { # torch::torch_is_installed() adj <- adj_from_edgelist(from = c(1, 2, 3, 4), to = c(2, 3, 4, 1)) x <- torch::torch_randn(4, 8)  layer <- layer_gcn(8, 4) layer(x, adj)  # Normalize once up front and reuse across layers adj_norm <- gcn_normalize(add_graph_self_loops(adj)) layer <- layer_gcn(8, 4, normalize = FALSE) layer(x, adj_norm) }

title: Generalized GCN Layer (Hamilton 2020) — layer_gcn_general
text: Implements single Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) layer following Hamilton 2020: $$\mathbf{H}^{(k)} = \sigma\left(\mathbf{}\mathbf{H}^{(k-1)}\mathbf{W}^{(k)}_{\text{neigh}} + \mathbf{H}^{(k-1)}\mathbf{W}^{(k)}_{\text{self}}\right)$$ can also written (Guo et al. 2025): $$\mathbf{X}^{(l)} = \sigma\left(\mathbf{D}^{-1}\mathbf{}\mathbf{X}^{(l-1)}\boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(l)} + \mathbf{X}^{(l-1)}\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{(l)} + \boldsymbol{\Psi}^{(l)}\right)$$ layer combines: Neighbor aggregation: \(D^{-1}AX^{(l-1)}\Theta^{(l)}\) Self transformation: \(X^{(l-1)}\Phi^{(l)}\) focal node transformation Global bias: \(\Psi^{(l)}\) additive bias term Parameters: \(\Theta\) (theta): in_features x out_features transforms aggregated neighbor features \(\Phi\) (phi): in_features x out_features transforms node's features \(\Psi\) (psi): out_features global bias term (shared across nodes)

title: Generalized GCN Layer (Hamilton 2020) — layer_gcn_general
code: layer_gcn_general(in_features, out_features, bias = TRUE, normalize = FALSE)

title: Generalized GCN Layer (Hamilton 2020) — layer_gcn_general
text: Tensor n_nodes x out_features. Transformed node features (activation)

title: Generalized GCN Layer (Hamilton 2020) — layer_gcn_general

what: Graph Isomorphism Network Layer (Xu et al. 2019) — layer_gin
title: Graph Isomorphism Network Layer (Xu et al. 2019) — layer_gin
text: Implements Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) layer: $$\mathbf{h}_i^{(k)} = \text{MLP}^{(k)}\left((1 + \epsilon^{(k)}) \cdot \mathbf{h}_i^{(k-1)} + \sum_{j \\mathcal{N}()} \mathbf{h}_j^{(k-1)}\right)$$ layer: Aggregates neighbor features via summation Adds weighted self features using learnable epsilon Applies MLP transformation Parameters: MLP: Multi-layer perceptron (typically 2 layers) epsilon: Learnable fixed weight self features

title: Graph Isomorphism Network Layer (Xu et al. 2019) — layer_gin

text: in_features Integer. Number input features per node out_features Integer. Number output features per node eps Numeric. Initial value epsilon. Default: 0 learn_eps Logical. Whether learn epsilon parameter. Default: FALSE

title: Graph Isomorphism Network Layer (Xu et al. 2019) — layer_gin
text: Tensor n_nodes x out_features. Transformed node features

title: Graph Isomorphism Network Layer (Xu et al. 2019) — layer_gin
text: MLP constructed sequence Linear-BatchNorm-ReLU-Linear layers. epsilon parameter can learned fixed 0.

title: Graph Isomorphism Network Layer (Xu et al. 2019) — layer_gin
text: layer(x, adj) x: Tensor n_nodes x in_features. Node feature matrix. adj: Sparse COO tensor n_nodes x n_nodes. Adjacency matrix defining graph structure.

title: Graph Isomorphism Network Layer (Xu et al. 2019) — layer_gin
text: Xu, K., Hu, W., Leskovec, J., & Jegelka, S. (2019). Powerful Graph Neural Networks? International Conference Learning Representations. doi:10.48550/arXiv.1810.00826

title: Graph Isomorphism Network Layer (Xu et al. 2019) — layer_gin
code: if (FALSE) { # torch::torch_is_installed() adj <- adj_from_edgelist(from = c(1, 2, 3, 4), to = c(2, 3, 4, 1)) x <- torch::torch_randn(4, 8)  layer <- layer_gin(8, 4) layer(x, adj)  # Learn the weight given to a node's own features layer <- layer_gin(8, 4, learn_eps = TRUE) layer(x, adj) }

title: Layer Normalization (Ba et al. 2016) — layer_layer_norm
text: Applies layer normalization node features: $$\mathbf{x}' = \frac{\mathbf{x} - \mathrm{E}[\mathbf{x}]}{\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}[\mathbf{x}] + \epsilon}} \odot \gamma + \beta$$ mean variance computed elements selected mode: "graph": statistics computed across nodes channels graph, giving single mean variance per graph. batch supplied, graph mini-batch normalized independently. "node": statistics computed across channels node independently, giving one mean variance per node.

title: Layer Normalization (Ba et al. 2016) — layer_layer_norm
code: layer_layer_norm(   in_features,   eps = 1e-05,   affine = TRUE,   mode = c("graph", "node") )

title: Layer Normalization (Ba et al. 2016) — layer_layer_norm
text: in_features Integer. Number input features per node eps Numeric. Value added denominator numerical stability. Default: 1e-5 affine Logical. TRUE, adds learnable scale shift parameters. Default: TRUE mode Character. Either "graph" "node". Default: "graph"

title: Layer Normalization (Ba et al. 2016) — layer_layer_norm
text: Tensor n_nodes x in_features. Normalized node features

title: Layer Normalization (Ba et al. 2016) — layer_layer_norm
text: "graph" mode removes graph-level location scale representation, makes useful inductive settings model trained one graph applied another. new graph's features degree distribution sit different scale, un-normalized layers propagate shift systematic bias predictions. "node" mode conventional layer normalization transformer architectures depend graph partition. Parameters (affine = TRUE): \(\gamma\): in_features learnable scale, initialized 1 \(\beta\): in_features learnable shift, initialized 0

title: Layer Normalization (Ba et al. 2016) — layer_layer_norm
text: layer(x, batch = NULL, batch_size = NULL) x: Tensor n_nodes x in_features. Node feature matrix. batch: Tensor NULL. Batch vector assigning node graph, using 1-based graph indices (e.g. c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2)). NULL, nodes treated belonging single graph. Ignored mode = "node". batch_size: Integer NULL. Number graphs. Calculated batch NULL.

title: Layer Normalization (Ba et al. 2016) — layer_layer_norm
text: Ba, J. L., Kiros, J. R., & Hinton, G. E. (2016). Layer normalization. doi:10.48550/arXiv.1607.06450

title: Layer Normalization (Ba et al. 2016) — layer_layer_norm
code: if (FALSE) { # torch::torch_is_installed() x <- torch::torch_randn(4, 16)  norm <- layer_layer_norm(16)  # Single graph norm(x)  # Mini-batch of graphs, normalized independently batch <- torch::torch_tensor(c(1, 1, 2, 2), dtype = torch::torch_long()) norm(x, batch = batch)  # Per-node normalization norm <- layer_layer_norm(16, mode = "node") norm(x) }

what: Regional GCN Convolutional Layer (Guo et al. 2025) — layer_regconv
title: Regional GCN Convolutional Layer (Guo et al. 2025) — layer_regconv
text: Implements Regional Graph Convolutional Network (RegConv) layer Guo et al. (2025): $$\mathbf{X}^{(l)} = \sigma\left(\left(\mathbf{D}^{-1}\mathbf{}\mathbf{X}^{(l-1)}\boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(l)} + \mathbf{X}^{(l-1)}\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{(l)}\right)\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{reg}^{(l)} + \boldsymbol{\Psi}_{reg}^{(l)}\right)$$ layer extends standard GCN layer introducing region-specific parameters handle spatial heterogeneity (spatial regimes). computation two stages: Base GCN transformation: \(\mathbf{D}^{-1}\mathbf{}\mathbf{X}^{(l-1)}\boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(l)} + \mathbf{X}^{(l-1)}\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{(l)}\) Region-specific modulation: Element-wise multiplication \(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{reg}\) addition \(\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{reg}\) Parameters: \(\Theta\) (theta): in_features x out_features transforms aggregated neighbor features (global) \(\Phi\) (phi): in_features x out_features transforms node's features (global) \(\Omega_{reg}\) (omega_reg): n_regions x out_features region-specific weight modulation \(\Psi_{reg}\) (psi_reg): n_regions x out_features region-specific bias terms

title: Regional GCN Convolutional Layer (Guo et al. 2025) — layer_regconv
text: RegConv layer designed two-stage training: Stage 1: Train global GCN learn \(\Theta\) \(\Phi\), freeze parameters. Stage 2: Initialize \(\Omega_{reg}\) 1s train region-specific parameters (\(\Omega_{reg}\), \(\Psi_{reg}\)) keeping \(\Theta\) \(\Phi\) fixed. region-specific parameters allow model adjust predictions differently across spatial regimes, enabling model capture spatial heterogeneity.

Adjacency matrix, expected row-normalized \(D^{-1}\) \(D\) degree matrix. Can binary weighted. region_assignments: Tensor n_nodes. Integer vector values 1:n_regions giving region node belongs . Multiple nodes can belong region. edge_weight: Tensor n_nodes x n_nodes NULL. Optional edge weights applied adjacency matrix. NULL, values adj used.

title: GraphSAGE Layer (Hamilton et al. 2017) — layer_sage
text: Implements GraphSAGE (Graph Sample Aggregate) layer: $$\mathbf{h}_{\mathcal{N}(v)}^{(k)} = \text{AGGREGATE}\left(\{\mathbf{h}_u^{(k-1)} : u \\mathcal{N}(v)\}\right)$$ $$\mathbf{h}_v^{(k)} = \sigma\left(\mathbf{W}^{(k)} \cdot \text{CONCAT}\left(\mathbf{h}_v^{(k-1)}, \mathbf{h}_{\mathcal{N}(v)}^{(k)}\right)\right)$$ layer: Aggregates neighbor features using specified aggregator Concatenates node's features aggregated neighbor features Applies linear transformation optional normalization Parameters: \(W\): (in_features + aggregated_features) x out_features learnable weight matrix \(b\): out_features learnable bias term (optional)

what: torchgnn: Graph Neural Networks for 'torch' — torchgnn-package
title: torchgnn: Graph Neural Networks for 'torch' — torchgnn-package
text: Build train graph neural networks top 'torch' deep learning framework. Message-passing layers provided Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) Kipf Welling (2017) doi:10.48550/arXiv.1609.02907 , GraphSAGE architecture Hamilton, Ying Leskovec (2017) doi:10.48550/arXiv.1706.02216 , Graph Attention Network (GAT) Velickovic others (2018) doi:10.48550/arXiv.1710.10903 , Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) Xu others (2019) doi:10.48550/arXiv.1810.00826 , regional GCN Guo others (2025) doi:10.1080/24694452.2025.2558661 . layers composed ready-made node-level graph-level models. Supporting utilities construct sparse adjacency matrices edge lists, normalize , pool node embeddings graph-level representations, split graphs training, validation test sets.

Multi-layer models: model_gcn(), model_gcn_general(), model_sage(), model_gat() model_gin(). Graph-level pooling pool_global_add(), pool_global_mean() pool_global_max(), normalization layer_layer_norm(). Graph construction preparation helpers: adj_from_edgelist(), nodes_to_tensor(), gcn_normalize(), adj_row_normalize(), add_graph_self_loops() graph_split().
